title: Cisco CCNA Automation 200-901 Study Guide
description: Automating Networks Using Cisco Platforms (200-901 CCNAAUTO) v1.0 earns the CCNA Automation certification. It is a 120-minute exam covering software development and design, APIs, application deployment and security, and infrastructure automation on Cisco platforms — the network-engineering side of DevOps rather than general programming. It costs $300 USD and is offered in English and Japanese.
audience: Network engineers whose work is drifting into scripting, developers building against network APIs, and automation or platform engineers in Cisco environments. It expects you to read and reason about Python, REST APIs, JSON and YAML, and version control — not to write production software, but enough that someone who has never scripted will find it hard going.
why_get_it: CCNA Automation proves you can bridge traditional networking and modern software automation—reading and writing Python, calling REST APIs, and automating infrastructure on Cisco platforms like DNA Center, Meraki, and ACI. That overlap is exactly what employers pay a premium for: network automation engineers consistently earn more than traditional network engineers at the same experience level. It is also the entry point to Cisco's Automation track (formerly DevNet), leading to CCNP Automation. For anyone in networking who wants to stay relevant as infrastructure becomes code-driven, this is the credential that signals you've made the jump.
when_to_get_it: Take it once you already understand networking and have started automating pieces of your own job — it assumes the network knowledge rather than teaching it, so CCNA first is the usual and sensible order. It suits people whose employer runs Cisco gear and is moving toward infrastructure-as-code, and it is the entry point into Cisco's automation track. If you want general automation skills rather than Cisco-specific ones, a Python and Git foundation plus a portfolio of real scripts will take you further for less money.
exam_format: Multiple-choice and multiple-response questions, 120 minutes, offered in English and Japanese. Cisco does not publish the question count or the passing score — third-party sites quoting "about 100 questions" or an "800–850 cut score" are guessing.
exam_questions: Cisco does not publish the question count
recertification_note: Valid for 3 years. Renew by passing another Cisco exam, earning Continuing Education credits through the Cisco CE program, or achieving a higher-level Cisco certification before expiration.
salary_note: Network automation is a premium niche. Engineers who combine networking with automation typically earn 15–30% more than traditional network engineers at the same level. Early-career roles blending networking and scripting commonly land around $75K–$95K; experienced network automation / NetDevOps engineers frequently reach $110K–$140K, with senior and cloud-heavy roles going higher. Demand is strongest where infrastructure is moving to code (large enterprises, service providers, cloud teams).

items: Python data structures, functions, and error handling
Code organization, modularity, and version control with Git
Common design patterns (MVC) and software development methods (agile, waterfall)
Parsing and constructing data formats: JSON, XML, YAML
Unit testing concepts
REST API principles: methods, status codes, and headers
Authentication mechanisms (basic, token, OAuth)
Constructing and interpreting API requests and responses
Rate limiting, pagination, and error handling
Webhooks and common API tools (Postman, curl, requests)
Cisco DNA Center, Meraki, and ACI APIs
Cisco Webex, Umbrella, and security platform APIs
Model-driven programmability (NETCONF, RESTCONF, YANG)
Network device APIs and configuration management
Cisco SDKs and the DevNet ecosystem
Deployment models: on-premises, private, public, and hybrid cloud
Containers and Docker fundamentals
CI/CD pipelines and DevOps concepts
Application security and the OWASP Top 10
Bug fixing, debugging, and logging
Controller-based vs device-level network management
Infrastructure as code and automation tools (Ansible, Puppet, Chef)
Automating configuration with APIs and scripts
CI/CD for network automation
Interpreting basic automation scripts and their outcomes
IP addressing, subnets, and common protocols
Networking devices: switches, routers, firewalls, load balancers
OSI and TCP/IP models
Network troubleshooting basics relevant to automation
How automation interacts with the data, control, and management planes

study_steps.title: Download the official 200-901 exam topics
study_steps.description: Get the official CCNAAUTO (200-901) exam topics from the Cisco Learning Network. The six domains and their weightings are your roadmap—review them before buying anything so you study what the exam actually tests.

study_steps.title: Get comfortable with Python basics
study_steps.description: The software development and API domains assume working Python: variables, data structures, functions, and the requests library. If you've never coded, start here. A free course like Kirk Byers' Python for Network Engineers is aimed squarely at this audience.

study_steps.title: Work through a primary video course
study_steps.description: Choose one comprehensive 200-901 course and complete it end to end. A full DevNet Associate / CCNA Automation course on Udemy covers all six domains with code walkthroughs. See the paid resources section for options.

study_steps.title: Read the official cert guide
study_steps.description: The Cisco Press DEVASC 200-901 Official Cert Guide is the Cisco-approved book for this exam. Use its 'Do I Know This Already?' quizzes and exam-prep tasks to find and close gaps in the API, platform, and automation chapters.

study_steps.title: Practice hands-on with Cisco DevNet
study_steps.description: This exam rewards real reps. Use the free Cisco DevNet Learning Labs and always-on Sandbox to call real Cisco platform APIs (DNA Center, Meraki, ACI). Practice REST calls in Postman and write small Python scripts that hit those APIs.

study_steps.title: Build small automation projects
study_steps.description: Reinforce the concepts by automating something concrete: pull device inventory via an API, push a config change with a script, or parse JSON/YAML output. Hands-on projects make the infrastructure-and-automation questions intuitive instead of abstract.

study_steps.title: Take timed practice exams
study_steps.description: Once you've covered all six domains, work through practice exams under timed conditions. Aim to score consistently above 85% before booking. Review every wrong answer until you understand the concept, not just the right option.

study_steps.title: Schedule and sit the exam
study_steps.description: Register through Pearson VUE and take the 120-minute exam at a test center or online proctored. Book about two weeks out to set a firm deadline. Get comfortable reading short code and API snippets quickly—several questions hinge on that.

faq.question: Is CCNA Automation the same as DevNet Associate?
faq.answer: Yes. As part of Cisco's 2026 certification rebrand, the Cisco Certified DevNet Associate was renamed CCNA Automation. The exam code (200-901) and core content are the same—only the name and some branding changed. You'll see both names used interchangeably for a while, and the DevNet developer platform itself keeps the DevNet name.

faq.question: Do I need to know how to code or program in Python?
faq.answer: Some Python is essential. The software development and API domains assume you can read and write basic Python—variables, data structures, functions, and the requests library. You don't need to be a software engineer, but a complete non-coder should budget extra time to build that foundation first.

faq.question: Is CCNA Automation good for beginners?
faq.answer: It's beginner-friendly for the automation path but assumes some networking and coding comfort. People with a networking background (CCNA-level) who are new to automation are the ideal audience. True beginners can do it, but should expect to learn networking basics and Python alongside the exam material.

faq.question: How hard is the 200-901 exam?
faq.answer: It's a genuine associate-level exam that spans two worlds—networking and software. The breadth is the challenge: you need working knowledge of Python, REST APIs, Cisco platform APIs, containers, CI/CD, and automation tools. Hands-on practice with the free Cisco DevNet labs makes a big difference.

faq.question: How long does it take to study for CCNA Automation?
faq.answer: Most candidates spend 2 to 4 months part-time. Those who already code or have DevOps experience may be ready in 6 to 8 weeks; networking pros new to programming should plan for the longer end while they build Python and API skills.

faq.question: Do I need CCNA (networking) first?
faq.answer: Not formally, and there's no prerequisite. But networking knowledge helps—the Network Fundamentals and Infrastructure and Automation domains assume you understand how networks work. Many people take CCNA first, then CCNA Automation to add programmability.

faq.question: What certification comes after CCNA Automation?
faq.answer: The natural Cisco progression is CCNP Automation (formerly DevNet Professional). Many automation engineers also branch into cloud (AWS, Azure), DevOps tooling, and infrastructure-as-code as they specialize.

faq.question: Does CCNA Automation expire?
faq.answer: Yes. Like all Cisco associate certifications, it's valid for three years. Renew it by passing another Cisco exam, earning Continuing Education credits through the Cisco CE program, or achieving a higher-level Cisco certification before it expires.

related_certs.title: Cisco CCNA
